quark_ponders.ponder.minecraft_chain.tex: Chains link blocks together when a piston moves them
The chain itself doesn't need to be moved by the piston, it attaches to the other moved blocks
Chains only link to blocks they visually connect to
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_chute.text_1: The Chute drops items straight down
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_chute.text_2: Hoppers, Droppers and other blocks can insert items into it
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_chute.text_3: Inserted items drop out underneath right away, always in the center
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_chute.text_4: A Flux signal disables the Chute
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_chute.text_5: A block placed under it disables it too
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_chute.text_6: The Chute can drop items through Hollow Logs and other blocks with a hole in the middle
quark_ponders.ponder.minecraft_dispenser: Dispensers can place blocks in the world
Blocks that already have a dispenser action, like Dynamite, keep using it
Blocks are placed facing forward from the dispenser
Crops such as wheat seeds and potatoes are planted the same way
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_ender_watcher: The Otherwatcher is a Flux input block
It gives off a Flux signal while a player is looking directly at it
The closer to the center the player looks, the stronger the signal
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_feeding_troug: The Feeding Trough holds food for animals
Animals within %s blocks are drawn to the right food and breed from it
Sometimes an animal needs more than one bite before it is ready to breed
If there are more than %s animals within %d blocks, they still eat but won't breed
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_gravisand.tex: Gravisand only falls when it receives a Flux signal
If it can't fall when powered, it floats upwards instead
The signal spreads to any touching Gravisand, so they fall or float together
Gravisand always gives a Flux Comparator a signal of 15
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_iron_rod.head: Iron Rod
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_iron_rod.text: An Iron Rod pushed by a piston works like a drill
It breaks most blocks in front of it
It only breaks blocks that a piston could push
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_metal_buttons: Gold and Iron Buttons are the button forms of Weighted Pressure Plates
Gold Buttons give a very short pulse, about a fifth of a second
Iron Buttons give a long pulse of 5 seconds
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_obsidian_pres: Obsidian Pressure Plates only trigger when a player steps on them
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_piston_move_t: Pistons can move blocks that hold things, like Chests and Furnaces
Moving one into a spot where it can't stay breaks it and drops its contents
For a block that pistons can't move, use Sturdy Stone
Some blocks, such as Monster Spawners, can't be moved this way
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_redstone_rand: The Flux Randomizer sends a signal out of a random side
When powered from the back, it randomly turns on either its left or right output
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_glass_item_fr: Glass Item Frames work like Item Frames but disappear once an item is placed in them
A banner placed in one lies flat against the wall, showing its pattern
Glass Item Frames can attach to the front of a standing Sign
The item then shows flush with the sign
Right-click through them to open chests and other containers
A map in a Glass Item Frame updates in real time
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_grate.text_1: The Iron Grate lets items fall through but stops mobs
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_grate.text_2: Farm animals won't walk over it
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_grate.text_3: Farm animals on a leash are not affected
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_grate.text_4: The Iron Grate can be waterlogged, and items float through it
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_grate.text_5: It can also be filled with lava
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_rope.text_1: Rope can be placed on the underside of a block by players and dispensers
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_rope.text_2: Right-click the rope with more rope, or use a dispenser, to extend it down
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_rope.text_3: Right-click with an empty hand or any other item to pull the rope up
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_rope.text_5: Rope can pull up and push down some blocks at its end
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_rope.text_6: Rope can be climbed like a ladder
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_stool.text_1: Stools bounce you when you fall on them, like beds
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_stool.text_3: A player sitting on a stool moves with it when a piston pushes or pulls it
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_stool.text_4: Placing a block above a stool makes it bigger, like a table
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_toretoise.tex: Oretoises are neutral mobs that spawn deep underground in complete darkness
Each Oretoise carries a random ore: Coal, Copper, Iron, Lapis or Flux
Hit an Oretoise with a pickaxe to make it drop its raw ore
Silk Touch makes it drop the ore block
Hitting an Oretoise without a pickaxe, or when it has no ore, sets off a shockwave
The shockwave hurts everything nearby except other Oretoises and turns their anger toward you
With care, an Oretoise can be brought home and fed so it regrows its ore
Oretoises can't ride in boats or be put on a leash
They can be carried in minecarts
Feeding an Oretoise Glow Berries sometimes makes it regrow its ore
The ore it regrows is random each time
A Feeding Trough can feed them to regrow their ore
After regrowing ore, an Oretoise won't eat again for %s seconds
Oretoises are 1 block tall, or 1.4 blocks tall while carrying ore
An Iron Rod pushed into an Oretoise by a piston breaks off its ore
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_foxhound.head: Foxhounds
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_foxhound.text: Foxhounds are hostile mobs that spawn in the Nether
They attack and set you on fire
Drink a potion of Fire Resistance and feed them Coal to tame them
Taming only works while you have Fire Resistance
Once tamed, they behave much like wolves
They sleep on hot blocks, like Magma Blocks or lit Furnaces
A Foxhound sleeping on a furnace makes it burn faster
Only one Foxhound can speed up a furnace at a time
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_skull_spike.t: Placing a Skeleton Skull, Zombie Head or Creeper Head on a fence makes a Skull Pike
Monsters within %s blocks that can see it will run away
Wither Skeleton Skulls and Dragon Heads don't work
Bosses and raiders are not scared off
Monsters already chasing a player may ignore the pikes
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_enhanced_ladd: Right-click a ladder with another ladder to place it below, so you can climb down safely
As long as the top ladder is supported, the ones below can hang freely
Looking down while on a ladder makes you slide down quickly
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_scaffolding_s: Right-click Scaffolding with a block to place it at the end of the scaffolding
It turns once, so blocks can be built sideways if the scaffolding extends that way
Sneak and right-click to place a block directly on the scaffolding
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_slimes_to_mag: When a large Slime dies on Magma Blocks, the slimes it splits into become Magma Cubes
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_pipe.text_1: Copper Pipes carry items from one place to another
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_pipe.text_2: Use a Hopper, Dropper or anything else that inserts items to put them into a pipe
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_pipe.text_3: At a junction, items keep going forward if they can
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_pipe.text_4: Otherwise, they turn left or right at random
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_pipe.text_5: A Flux signal disables a pipe, and items won't flow into powered pipes
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_pipe.text_6: When items can't go any other way, they go up
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_pipe.text_7: Items always go down whenever they can
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_pipe.text_8: Items can flow into and out of pipes
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_pipe.text_9: A Flux Comparator reads how many items are in a pipe, one level per stack inside
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_pipe.text_10: A pipe holding more than %s stacks, or that many different items, breaks and drops them
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_pipe.text_11: Pipes can be encased in glass, which is only for looks
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_magnet.text_1: Magnets move metal blocks, meaning blocks made of Iron or Copper
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_magnet.text_2: This includes anything made from Iron or Copper
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_magnet.text_5: When several Magnets act on the same block, the strongest one wins
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_magnet.text_6: A magnet's force on a block is its Flux level minus the distance
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_magnet.text_7: Creatures made of or wearing magnetic materials are moved by magnets too
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_magnet.text_8: A Hopper moved by a magnet drops one of its items in front of it
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_magnet.text_9: If that item is a seed, it plants it in front or one block down
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_magnet.text_1: A Stonecutter moved by a magnet breaks the block above it%s
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_magnet.silk: as if mined with Silk Touch
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_magnet.text_1: Very hard blocks such as Obsidian can't be broken this way
An Iron Rod moved by a magnet breaks the block in front of it
Very hard blocks such as Obsidian can't be broken this way
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_influence.tex: Lit candles influence which enchantments appear in the Matrix Enchanter, by up to %s%%
Each candle colour influences a different set of enchantments, shown in EMI
This Lime Candle makes %s more likely to appear%s
Candles can be turned into soul candles
Soul candles reverse the effect, making those enchantments less likely to appear
Candles also become soul candles when a soul block is under the bookshelves
Lit candles give the same enchanting power as a bookshelf
This setup still gives full enchanting power
